statement: On any finite undirected graph G with an a-b path and x>0, the x^length-weighted vertex-simple a-b path avoids A (excluding a,b) with probability Z_(G minus A)(a,b)/Z_G(a,b). Revealing its prefix gives M_n=1{prefix avoids A} Z_(H_n minus A)(v_n,b)/Z_H_n(v_n,b), where H_n deletes all previously visited vertices except the tip. M_n is a bounded martingale equal to the conditional expectation of complete avoidance.
proof_or_counterexample: Cancel the common x^n prefix factor in each compatible completion. The remaining normalized tail measure gives the conditional avoidance probability. Conditional-expectation tower property proves the martingale.
independent_reviewer: w401; KEEP at exact scope; RECEIVED_W401_VERDICTS.jsonl
remaining_gap: No continuum asymptotic or SAW regularity estimate follows from this identity.

statement: For a capacity-2 chordal Loewner chain driven by dW=mu dt+dN with continuous local martingale N and d<N>=v dt, fix constant alpha>0. Before three fixed obstacles are hit, let their hydrodynamic conformal maps h_i be analytic at W with h_i'(W)>0. If M_i=h_i'(W)^alpha are local martingales on a common positive interval and the matrix J with rows (h_i''/h_i',h_i'''/h_i',(h_i''/h_i')^2) is invertible for a.e. time there, then mu=0 and v=8/3 a.e. there, and alpha=5/8. A global SLE identification additionally requires coverage of all finite times by such intervals.
assumptions: Continuous Loewner driver with absolutely continuous drift and quadratic variation
Analytic reflection and positive map derivative near W
Three local martingales on an interval, not just pointwise initial drift tests
proof_or_counterexample: Commuting-map Taylor expansion and Ito give normalized drift e=J(mu,v/2-4/3,[1+v(alpha-1)]/2). Each local martingale has zero finite-variation density; invert J. Three vertical slits (1,1),(-1,1),(1,3) have initial determinant 9/32 and by continuity give a positive initial localization interval.
independent_reviewer: w401; KEEP at exact scope; RECEIVED_W401_VERDICTS.jsonl
remaining_gap: Hardest: conditional SAW partition martingales must converge uniformly in localized random slit domains to these powers with a common alpha. Driver regularity and global probe coverage are also unproved.

If v>=v_min>0, also |alpha-5/8|<=(31/(2v_min))epsilon. The inverse matrix norm is 20/3.

statement: Let X be a compact metric space and K_m,K random nonempty compact sets with K_m converging in law to K in Hausdorff distance. For a nonempty closed A, set p_m(r)=P(K_m avoids {x:dist(x,A)<=r}). If p_m(0) tends to q and there are r_j decreasing to 0 with p_m(r_j) tending to q_j for every j and q_j tending to q, then P(K avoids A)=q.
assumptions: Both unbuffered and buffer-stable avoidance limits
proof_or_counterexample: Distance from a compact set to A is continuous under Hausdorff convergence. Open Portmanteau gives P(distance>0)<=q. Closed Portmanteau gives q_j<=P(distance>=r_j)<=P(distance>0); pass j to infinity.

remaining_gap: No buffer-stable SAW partition asymptotic has been proved; no curve-topology consequence is inferred.

statement: On the honeycomb six-cycle with endpoints 0 and 3 and weights x^length, x>0, avoidance of vertex 1 and avoidance of vertex 5 each have probability 1/2 but their intersection has probability 0. Avoidance of vertices 1 and 2 has joint probability 1/2. Thus finite-SAW obstacle avoidance has neither universal independence nor a universal sign of association.
proof_or_counterexample: There are exactly two simple endpoint paths, each of length three and equal weight. Opposite-branch deletion excludes both; two same-branch deletions leave the other branch. Products of individual probabilities are 1/4 in both cases.

Consequently simple limiting traces alone do not imply convergence of oriented curves or injective curve limits.
